relational_axes.axis_name: From lonely witness to allied reformer
relational_axes.pole_start: He begins as a morally serious but relatively isolated witness who needs allies to make his case heard.
relational_axes.pole_end: He ends as part of a reformist moral community, marked by admiration, solidarity, and shared anti-slavery purpose.

trajectory.position_description: He identifies and values people whose conduct aligns with his moral convictions, especially those who support him sincerely.
key_moments: Warm admiration for Quakers and abolitionist allies

trajectory.position_description: His relationship to abolitionist allies becomes collective and political through petitions, Sierra Leone support, and public argument.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: This axis captures a communal dimension not explicit in Set A: Gustavus’s growing solidarity with reform-minded allies gives his witness a collective political form.

structuralist.label: Structuralist / Narratologist
structuralist.reasoning: Published scholarship does support reading Equiano’s narrative as moving from an isolated witness to a figure embedded in abolitionist and Quaker networks. Critics have noted that the text strategically stages his credibility through patronage, testimony, and alliance-building, especially in relation to Quaker abolitionists such as the Gurneys and other reform-minded readers. This makes the axis of lonely witness becoming an allied reformer well grounded in the scholarship.
